mathcounts-potw-2026-08-31-01.title: Area formula
mathcounts-potw-2026-08-31-01.body:
Medium: $r = 5.5$, $A = \pi(5.5)^2 = 30.25\pi \approx 95.03$ in². Large: $r = 8.25$, $A = \pi(8.25)^2 = 68.0625\pi \approx 213.82$ in².

**Answer: medium ≈ 95.03 in², large ≈ 213.82 in²**

mathcounts-potw-2026-08-31-01.title: Scale the medium
mathcounts-potw-2026-08-31-01.body:
The large diameter is $16.5 \div 11 = 1.5$ times the medium's, so its area is $1.5^2 = 2.25$ times: $30.25\pi \times 2.25 = 68.0625\pi \approx 213.82$ in², with medium $30.25\pi \approx 95.03$ in².

**Answer: medium ≈ 95.03 in², large ≈ 213.82 in²**

mathcounts-potw-2026-08-31-02.title: Area needed
mathcounts-potw-2026-08-31-02.body:
Large area $\approx 213.82$ in², so one large slice $\approx 13.36$ in². Twenty large slices (2 for each of 10 members) $\approx 267.28$ in². A medium has $\approx 95.03$ in²: $267.28 \div 95.03 \approx 2.81$, so **3 medium** pizzas. Large: 20 slices $\div$ 16 per pizza $= 1.25$, so **2 large** pizzas.

**Answer: 3 medium or 2 large**

mathcounts-potw-2026-08-31-02.title: Compare in large-pizza units
mathcounts-potw-2026-08-31-02.body:
They need $\frac{20}{16} = 1.25$ large pizzas' worth of area. A medium is $\left(\frac{11}{16.5}\right)^2 = \frac49$ of a large. Medium pizzas needed: $1.25 \div \frac49 = 2.8125$, so 3. Large: $1.25 \to 2$.

**Answer: 3 medium or 2 large**

mathcounts-potw-2026-08-31-03.title: Price per square inch
mathcounts-potw-2026-08-31-03.body:
3 medium: $10.99 + 5 + 5 = \$20.99$ for $3 \times 95.03 = 285.09$ in²: about \$0.074 per in².
2 large: $15.99 + 5 = \$20.99$ for $2 \times 213.82 = 427.64$ in²: about \$0.049 per in².
Same cost, more pizza: **2 large pizzas**.

**Answer: 2 large pizzas**

mathcounts-potw-2026-08-31-03.title: Same price, compare area
mathcounts-potw-2026-08-31-03.body:
Both options cost exactly \$20.99, so the better deal is the one with more area. Two larges have $2 \times 2.25 = 4.5$ medium-pizzas' worth of area versus 3 for the mediums.

**Answer: 2 large pizzas**
